new_statements.quote: 1.2.12. Stress. Primary stress, [ˊ], occurs on either the penult or ultima and is not predictable in terms of any other phonological feature. [ʔámʌ] /ʔáma/ 'father'; [núʌŋg] /núang/ 'carabao'; [pfʌlé] /balé/ 'house'; [ʔumé] /ʔumé 'go.' Secondary stress [ˋ] is predictable in terms of primary stress. When primary stress falls on the ultima, secondary stress is found on the antepenult of polysyllabic words. [hìnʌmʌ́r] /hìnamál/ 'cooked rice'; [ʔìtulúd] /ʔìtulúd/ 'accompany and return'; [hʌ̀kʌtšʔú] /hàgadʔú/ 'my broom'; [ʔʌ̀witɔ́ʌn] /ʔàwitón/ 'get (a person)'.
new_statements.citation: Newell, Leonard E. 1956. Phonology of the Guhang Ifugao dialect. Philippine Journal of Science 85(4): 523-539.
new_statements.locator: p. 532, sec. 1.2.12 'Stress' (see also p. 523 'There is a suprasegmental phoneme of stress' and p. 527, sec. 1.1.19 'Stress Placement' minimal pairs)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (17 pp., IA scanned layer; PDF p.1 = printed p.523, PDF p.10 = printed p.532, confirmed by running heads) and rendered PDF pp. 1, 5, 10 to PNG and read them. PDF p.10 / printed p.532 carries sec. 1.2.12 "Stress" exactly as quoted: "Primary stress, [ˊ], occurs on either the penult or ultima and is not predictable in terms of any other phonological feature.... Secondary stress [ˋ] is predictable in terms of primary stress. When primary stress falls on the ultima, secondary stress is found on the antepenult of polysyllabic words." The English prose is verbatim; the only differences are in the rendering of the 1956 phonetic symbols in the examples (e.g. the page's [ʔʌ̀witɔ́ˆn] vs the rep…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is phonemic and lexically fixed on one of the last two syllables: primary stress falls on either the penult or the ultima and cannot be predicted from any other phonological property (minimal pairs such as /nahílong/ 'look in awe' vs /nahilóng/ 'was dark', /ʔumáli/ 'come' vs /ʔumalí/ 'call', /ʔánon/ 'remove' vs /ʔanón/ 'eat').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Predictable from primary stress: when primary stress is on the ultima, secondary stress falls on the antepenult of polysyllabic words (/hìnamál/, /ʔìtulúd/, /hàgadʔú/, /ʔàwitón/).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Newell adds (p. 533) that in the informant's practical spelling stress is omitted 'except when stress placement is the minimal difference between two lexically different words'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonemic analysis of isolated lexical items (citation forms) and derived words, based on one speaker from Guhang village, Banaue, data 1954-1955; the analysis also states that every syllable peak receives 'syllable stress' (p. 535, sec. 2.1), a syllable-definition notion distinct from the word-level primary/secondary stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Newell 1956 describes the dialect of Guhang village, Banaue, which he says "varies only slightly from the Banaue Central dialect and may be considered as part of the larger Banaue dialect" (p. 523); Glottolog 5.1 files this article under amga1235 (Amganad Ifugao = Banaue-area Ifugao, Ethnologue dialects Banaue Ifugao, Burnay Ifugao). Newell's later work is on Batad Ifugao (bata1298), a different language. The Reid 1971 sketch labelled "Ifugao, Amganad" (from Goetz 1963) is the variety-named source but its stress text was not obtainable.
